sources.note: Call for Applications, Mauritius Africa Scholarship Scheme 2026, Republic of Mauritius, dated October 2025. This is the record's official_source_url. Downloaded and text-extracted in full; 1 page.

Mauritius Africa Scholarship Scheme programme page on the Ministry's own site, the page the Call points applicants to. Fetched live on 12 Oct 2026 (HTTP 200); it publishes the 'Edition 2026' document set and an 'Archive 2025' set, and contains no 2027 edition.
Guidelines for Applicants - Diploma and Undergraduate degree, MASS 2026, Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research. Read in full (9 pages) for eligibility, funding and degree-level terms.
Guidelines for Applicants - MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD, MASS 2026. Read in full (10 pages) for the postgraduate age limit, qualification and funding terms.

awarding_body.detail: The awarding body is the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research of the Republic of Mauritius, exactly as the record states. The Call names the Ministry as the destination for applications and the decision-maker, and the Guidelines are headed with the same Ministry name. Note a minor inconsistency inside the Ministry's own documents: the Call's postal block reads 'Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Technology' while the running header, the Guidelines and the submission instruction all read 'Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research'.
awarding_body.quote: Applications and all supporting documents must be forwarded to the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research of the Republic of Mauritius at the address mentioned below for the final selection.

deadline.detail: The record claims 'No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline'. The applicant-facing guidelines do support that for the applicant's own submission ('a deadline to be determined by the Nominating Agency'), but the Call for Applications and the Nominating Agency Guidelines both publish a central date for the 2026 edition: 27 March 2026. That date has passed (today is 12 October 2026). The Education Institution application windows in Section 8 of the Guidelines are also all closed (01 October 2025 to 27 February 2026, or November/December 2025 to February/March 2026), for an academic year stated to start August/October 2026. The live MASS page shows only 'Edition 2026' plus 'Archive 2025' and no 2027 edition, so there is no currently-open cycle.
deadline.quote: Such Nominating Agency, which may typically be part of the Ministry of Education in the country of the applicant, will then shortlist and endorse the applications of a maximum of FIFTEEN (15) eligible candidates (the decision on the distribution of nominees from the undergraduate and/or postgraduate programmes rest on the nominating agencies) and submit the duly completed application forms by 27 March 2026

eligibility.detail: Every distinct eligibility claim in the record is confirmed. Nationality: resident citizens of African Union member states or African Commonwealth countries, and Mauritian nationals are explicitly excluded. Age: above 18 and under 26 at 01 January 2027 for undergraduate, under 40 at 01 January 2027 for MPhil/MPhil-PhD/PhD, i.e. 1 January of the intake year as the record states. Qualification: the record's 'about 60% or 12/20' is confirmed as one of the accepted routes for the undergraduate degree, and the postgraduate route uses the same threshold; the Call's Section 8 institution list confirms the requirement to hold or be applying for a place at a listed Mauritian public HEI.
eligibility.quote: The Government of Mauritius invites applications from deserving students who are resident citizens of member states of the African Union or African Commonwealth countries for the Mauritius Africa Scholarship Scheme, as per the following criteria: 1. For undergraduate programmes, applicants should be above 18 years of age and should not have reached their 26th birthday by 01 January 2027. 2. For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes, applicants should not have reached their 40th birthday by 01 January 2027.

funding.detail: The funding claim 'Partially Funded' is confirmed, and the record is right not to call it fully funded. The award pays tuition and study-related costs only up to a cap (MUR 100,000 for SADC-country beneficiaries at local rates, MUR 160,000 for non-SADC at international rates) and any excess is borne by the awardee. The living support is explicitly described as partial: a monthly allowance of MUR 16,500 paid 'as part support', with students expected to top it up. Return airfare by the most economical route is covered, but reimbursed rather than paid up front. Books, overseas fieldwork, examination re-sits and repeat years are all at the awardee's cost.
funding.quote: The Scholarship will support successful candidates in meeting their tuition fees and contributing to their living expenses during their studies in Mauritius. Furthermore, the scholarship covers return airfare by the most economical route.

degree_levels.detail: The record's 'Undergraduate Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil, PhD' matches the Call's own duration table, which lists Undergraduate Diploma, Undergraduate Degree (i.e. Bachelor's), MPhil, PhD and additionally a combined MPhil/PhD route that the record's list omits. The route exists in the Guidelines too, so this is an omission in the record's list rather than a contradiction.
degree_levels.quote: 1 Undergraduate Diploma Three (3) years 2 Undergraduate Degree Four (4) years 3 MPhil Two (2) years + 6 months for thesis defence 4 MPhil / PhD Three (3) years + 6 months for approval of transfer report and One (1) year + 6 months for thesis defence 5 PhD Three (3) years + 6 months for thesis defence

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Applicants submit through their country's Nominating Agency by a deadline that Nominating Agency sets ('This should be done by a deadline to be determined by the Nominating Agency and communicated to prospective applicants'), while the Ministry itself sets one central closing date per edition: for MASS 2026 (July/September 2026 intake) the Call for Applications required nominating agencies to 'submit the duly completed application forms by 27 March 2026'. That date is past; no 2027 edition was published as at 12 October 2026.
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Deadline 2026-03-27 belongs to the closed MASS 2026 edition and must not be shown as an open deadline. As at 12 October 2026 the live Ministry MASS page publishes only 'Edition 2026' and 'Archive 2025' with no 2027 call, so the programme has no currently-open cycle. The HEI application windows in Section 8 of the 2026 Guidelines also closed between 27 February and end of March 2026. Re-check from late October 2026 onward, when the 2027 edition is expected to appear on https://tertiaryeducation.govmu.org/te/index.php/mass/ on the historical annual pattern. Also worth a field fix: the degree_levels list is missing the combined 'MPhil/PhD' route. A reviewer should decide whether an 'open/closed' flag is needed, since every MASS edition runs a roughly October-to-March window and the record is otherwise accurate.

notes_for_reviewer: The record is factually right on awarding body, eligibility, funding and degree levels; the single material problem is the deadline. Its label states no central date is published, but the awarding body's own Call for Applications publishes 27 March 2026 for the 2026 edition, and that cycle is closed. Because there is no currently-open cycle and no 2027 edition has been posted, the record must not be flipped to active. Two human decisions: (1) whether to keep the record listed at all while closed, or to hide it until the 2027 call appears, and (2) the canonical URL - the recorded one is a 2026-edition PDF that will be replaced by a new path, whereas https://tertiaryeducation.govmu.org/te/index.php/mass/ is stable across editions. One caveat on my evidence: quotes were taken from text extraction of the PDFs, where the extraction inserts stray spaces inside words (e.g. 'Af rican', 'th e'); I have quoted the page as it reads visually.
